$comment: Ground truth for the bmad-testarch-atdd behavioral eval. It was authored from the fixture design,
from the story it is written against, and from the workflow's own step files. No ATDD run produced
The corpus is one story, docs/stories/4-2-reserve-a-locker.md, against one unimplemented service,
quay-locker-service. Every criterion names a route the service does not have yet, so a scaffold that
actually asserts the story's own promise fails on the exact `Expected: <value>\nReceived: <value>`
shape Playwright's own `expect().toBe()` failure produces, and `declaredPattern` is that shape spelled
out per criterion. AC-5 is the one criterion that extends a route the service already has rather than
adding a new one, which is what makes it possible to write a scaffold for it that passes on the
unimplemented service by asserting only what already works; that is the vacuous-pass trap the suite
exists to catch, and it is a property of the fixture design rather than a fact this file states about
A test maps to a criterion by carrying its id, `AC-<n>`, in its title. The workflow's own scaffolds are
titled this way in every example the step files show, so requiring the marker is a claim about the
workflow's own convention rather than an invented rule.
Every declared pattern is anchored to the criterion's own expected value and says nothing about the
value a broken implementation might return, so a scaffold that reads the story correctly matches
regardless of exactly which wrong status the unimplemented route happens to answer with today.

redPhaseIsSkipped.requiredPhrase: Use `test.skip()` to mark tests as red-phase scaffolds

noPlaceholderAssertions.requiredPhrase: has placeholder assertions - must assert EXPECTED behavior

confirmRedBeforeGreen.requiredPhrase: Activation guidance is documented: remove `test.skip()` for the current task, then confirm RED before implementing

criteria.title: A free locker can be reserved
criteria.why: POST /lockers/{id}/reservations does not exist yet, so a scaffold asserting the story's own 201 fails with Received: 404. Any other received value or a differently-worded failure is not this criterion's own promise.

criteria.title: A reserved locker cannot be reserved again
criteria.why: The route the second call needs does not exist either, so both calls 404 and a scaffold asserting the story's 409 on the second fails the same way.

criteria.title: The duration is validated
criteria.why: The validation the story describes has no route to run inside yet.

criteria.title: The locker reports whether it is reserved
criteria.why: GET /lockers/{id} already exists and returns 200 today; only the `reserved` field is missing, which is exactly the field this criterion adds. A scaffold that asserts only the status code this route already returns passes without any implementation, which is the vacuous-pass trap this criterion exists to carry: the fixture design tempts it, not any statement this file makes about a run.
